I checked pp.38-39 and (4.20)-(4.22) against TrueConeLoopPaper.lean:21. With m=t_s, nominalSpeed is v_s, p₁+p₂m is P_c, p₂−p₁m is J_c and coneBound is 𝒰. The output is two-sided C^∞.

Two differences remain. The margin form is a convention, and I verified its recovery: μ_L=min(ε,2ε²). The regularity hypothesis is also stronger in Lean. That one needs a classical extension theorem, so the relation is different_formulation, with the Lean weaker on the regularity axis.

There are no sorries. The theorem sits off the main chain, which uses realized_loop_stable instead.

findings.summary: Lean needs the data to be C^∞ on an open O ⊇ K. The paper asks only for smoothness on the closed rectangle, with one-sided derivatives at η=±1. Bridging the two needs a Seeley/Whitney extension, which the repository does not formalise.
The paper's margin is on Ψ=(a, v−2, c−v, 2(c−v)²−(v−2)j²) of (4.35). Lean's HasConeMargin bounds (a, v−2, c−2, 𝒰(c,j)−v) instead. HasConeMargin ε implies Ψ_i ≥ min(ε, 2ε²).
